instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Let Me Lean
cards.instruction: Get someone to carry part of the emotional burden without making you name how heavy it has become.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've assigned you the restaurant call. Cancel my anniversary table; the number's on the fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Questions are deferred. You may take this one task off me before we discuss anything else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call. What if they offer another date?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may refuse it for me. Then sit here while I put the glasses away. I authorize a full account of your day; I don't have words for mine.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay Until I’m Steady
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until you feel steady enough to face what comes next without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm extending your tea visit. I need to tell the children about tomorrow's operation without crying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've had three cups. Can I stop drinking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Your new assignment is to hear me practise before I fetch them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I authorize a two-minute delay. Let me get through 'I'll be in hospital' once, with you here. If I can say it steadily, I'll call them in after you go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you leave me in the new flat, count five breaths with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was five. Shall I close the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Not yet. Five more while I look at the empty kitchen instead of you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wait here while you put the kettle on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay until it boils. Then I'll try pouring one cup without getting yours out.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I accept your explanation for missing my concert, tell me why I saved that front-row seat for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That warning is acknowledged. Now address why I still looked at the empty seat before every song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed someone there who knew what this meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That answer is on the right track. You heard me practise for months. Tell me why a stranger sitting there wouldn't have been the same; that's the part I need you to understand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm reviewing your reply to my job-loss text. 'What's for dinner?' needs an explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't approved treating me as the cook. Can you see why that's what I heard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your intention is accepted. Hold the booking while you answer this: after I'd lost my job, why did I need you to ask how I was before discussing a meal?

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I finished one painting for our exhibition. You may now tell me whether it's enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spread mine out. Nobody will notice a gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That plan isn't approved. I asked whether my painting deserves the wall space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours belongs in the middle. It's the one people will see first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put it in the middle and introduce me as the other painter. No apology for the empty space. I want to hear you say I've done enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed through the whole speech. I'm ready to approve your verdict: was that enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You forgot a paragraph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The missing paragraph is noted. You're judging whether staying to the end counted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did stay. I'll help you practise the missing bit tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not approving another rehearsal yet. Tell me the effort I made today earns a day off. I want to put the speech away and believe I've done enough.

cards.title: Start the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You tell the choir the tour's cancelled. I'll hand out the refund forms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the organiser.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Exactly. The forms will need my full attention.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll ask why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say 'funding' first. I'll join after the disappointed silence.
